flash_696037.description:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday re-shared his post of endorsement of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from a week ago.

"To the people of Israel, to those who haven’t seen it, I am attaching the Endorsement I gave one week ago to your Prime Minister, Bibi Netanyahu. As everyone is aware, including the enemy, Bibi and I have had a great relationship in winning together. I did the Venezuelan attack, one of the most successful Military Operations in History but, before that, we did Operation Midnight Hammer, stopping the World’s Number One State Sponsor of Terror from obtaining a Nuclear Weapon. Then we did Operation Epic Fury, and Iran now has No Navy, No Air Force, and both their Military and Economy are in shambles, including the fact that Iran’s Inflation is at 301%. The Naval Blockade has precluded them from getting Oil, and two levels of leadership, both Military and otherwise, are gone," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social.

He added, "When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi has been an outstanding Warrior Prime Minister! Israel was called The Little Satan, with the United States being called The Big Satan, by some very evil people. There can no longer be the chant heard around the World of 'Death to America, Death to Israel,' and there won’t be. Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!"

flash_696036.description:
The Yashar party has contacted the Central Elections Committee following the circulation of messages that it says falsely appear to be official communications from the party, using its name and the phone number designated for unsubscribing from its mailing list.

The party stated: "In recent hours, fake and misleading messages have been circulated, impersonating official communications from the Yashar party and using the party's name and unsubscribe phone number. We have demanded that the Central Elections Committee exercise its full authority, including an investigation by its cyber department, to identify those responsible and prevent such incidents from happening again."

flash_696035.description: Police Commissioner Danny Levy presents Israel's Election Day security plan to Justice Noam Sohlberg, with more than 20,000 officers set to deploy nationwide.

flash_696045.description: After ruling out US strikes on Iran on Sunday, Trump says he is willing to take time to secure a nuclear agreement and warns of the dangers of a nuclear-armed Tehran.

flash_696044.description:
Flavio Bolsonaro, who lost the Brazilian presidential runoff to incumbent president Lula da Silva, stated that he refused to accept the results of the election.

“It is impossible to recognize the election results in the context of how these things happened. We are going to use our legal team, we are going to request the annulment of these elections," he stated.

Bolsonaro criticized the extension of voting hours, saying that "the extension of voting hours was unacceptable." Lula's victory has been attributed in part to high voter turnout in the second round.

flash_696042.description: The Saudi-led military coalition announced early this morning that it intercepted a ballistic missile launched by Houthi rebels in Yemen toward the Saudi capital, Riyadh.

flash_696040.description: Brazilian President Lula da Silva wins a fourth term, defeating pro-Israel rival Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff.

flash_696038.description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva holds a narrow lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round of the presidential election.

With 80% of the votes counted, Lula has received 51.25% of the vote, compared to 48.75% for Bolsonaro.

flash_696062.description: Over 130 British doctors looking to move to Israel attended the MedEx UK event in London on Sunday.

flash_696061.description: Four senior reserve officers who served alongside Ofer Winter urge him to withdraw from elections, warning his party could waste crucial votes, cost right-wing bloc its majority.

flash_696060.description: CNN claims Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sought joint US-Israeli attack on Iran before elections, failed to secure US President Donald Trump's approval. Prime Minister's Office: Fake news.

flash_696058.description: Defense Minister Israel Katz denies reports of disagreements between the government and IDF over Iran, saying no plans to launch attack before elections.

flash_696056.description: After weeks of controversy, a judge ordered the release of Samaria security coordinator Pinchas Ran to house arrest.

flash_696054.description: A new policy blueprint urges Israel's next government to advance a sweeping slate of legislative reforms.

flash_696052.description: Israel’s enemies are waiting for there to be just one government which is “temporarily focussed on the Hareidi issue," on fighting internally instead of fighting them. Remember the days of Oslo and the "peace camp"? Opinion.

flash_696050.description: CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper visits the Strait of Hormuz as US forces report helping more than 3,000 ships transit the waterway and keeping shipping lanes clear of Iranian mines.

flash_696048.description: NYPD arrests a Brooklyn woman after a Jewish rabbinical student was stabbed in Manhattan's Diamond District.

flash_696046.description: Britain's Board of Deputies declares the Green Party racist over its anti-Zionist policy, urging other parties to reject cooperation unless the resolution is reversed.

flash_696043.description: Trump criticizes Jewish voters backing Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, whose statements on Israel and response to a synagogue attack have drawn controversy.

flash_696041.description: During talks on an alliance with Yaron Zelekha, Moshe Feiglin reportedly said he could support Gadi Eisenkot as Prime Minister if appointed Defense Minister.

flash_696039.description:
Incumbent Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is expected to win another term after widening his lead over his rival in the second round of the presidential election.

With 96% of the votes counted, Lula has received 51.73% of the vote, compared to 48.27% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

flash_696084.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin is expected to meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Moscow tomorrow. The two are also expected to meet with the Emir of Qatar later.

flash_696083.description: Chelli Goldenberg made harsh remarks about "the occupation and the settlers," only to discover that the conversation had been broadcast live. "I thought we were on a commercial break," she said.

flash_696081.description: Saudi military spokesman Turki al-Maliki announced that the Saudi military intercepted three unmanned aerial vehicles in the area of ​​the capital Riyadh and in the south of the kingdom.

flash_696079.description:
Hezbollah has been preparing for the renewal of Israeli attacks over the past three months, while at the same time receiving tens of millions of dollars from Iran to restore its military capabilities, according to a report by the Reuters news agency.

Sources in Lebanon said that the organization is also working to rehabilitate its top leadership. Earlier this month, Reuters reported that Iran had transferred about $200 million to Hezbollah for military rehabilitation purposes.

flash_696078.description: A teenage girl with no underlying medical conditions is hospitalized in intensive care at Assuta Ashdod Hospital following a severe complication of influenza. Her condition deteriorated within hours, and she is now sedated and on a ventilator.

flash_696076.description: You don't need perfect Hebrew or political connections to have a voice in this country. Opinion.

flash_696074.description: UN-appointed inquiry alleges extermination in Judea and Samaria and genocide in Gaza; Israeli mission accuses investigators of distorting history.

flash_696072.description: The problem isn't representing the voters. it's the ability to govern effectively. Opinion.

flash_696070.description: Israel signs defense deal to supply Cyprus with new patrol vessel equipped with advanced Rafael naval systems, upgrade an existing vessel.

flash_696068.description: The State Prosecutor's Office filed an indictment on Monday against an Israeli attorney accused of maintaining contact with a foreign agent and obstructing an investigation.

flash_696066.description: Lana Nusseibeh, a senior Emirati diplomat of Palestinian descent, has entered the race to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations.

flash_696064.description: Paratroopers arrest five Hamas and Islamic Jihad terrorists in Qabatiya; Battalion 202 raids over 50 locations in Binyamin during separate counterterrorism operation.

flash_696059.description: Sheffi Paz, a prominent activist who led the struggle on behalf of South Tel Aviv residents and against illegal immigration, died Monday morning at the age of 74.

flash_696057.description: Israeli security forces arrest three suspects, including one with suspected Hamas ties, in operations in Bethlehem and Hebron.

flash_696055.description: The problem isn't representing the voters. It's the ability to govern effectively. Opinion.

flash_696097.description: In a special lecture ahead of the elections, Rabbi Dudi Dudkevitch emphasized that voting is not merely a civic right, but a Torah obligation and a responsibility toward the future of the country.

flash_696096.description: Jordanian fighter jets strike terrorist hideouts in southern Syria after a deadly church funeral shooting killed nine people and wounded 34.

flash_696094.description: Ahead of Israel's Knesset elections, find out where and when to vote, what identification to bring, which rides are free, and when results are expected.

flash_696092.description: Captivity survivor Agam Berger criticized a campaign video released by Yair Golan's Democrats Party that combined footage of the October 7 attacks with political messages.

flash_696090.description: The IDF eliminated four Hamas and Islamic Jihad terrorists in strikes across the Gaza Strip over the weekend, including a Hamas Nukhba cell commander and a sniper who targeted Israeli troops.

flash_696088.description: if you insist on applying the Venezuelan model to Iran, Mr. President, history may remember you not for completing the struggle against Islamic terrorism, but for leaving that struggle unfinished. Opinion.

flash_696086.description: The next time you are offered the opportunity to join a new Jewish community in America with glatt kosher restaurants and bakeries, magnificent shuls, luxurious mikvahs, affordable villas, and all the comforts of your dreams, think twice.

flash_696082.description: After IDF troops identified three terrorists exiting a tunnel shaft in Khan Yunis, an aircraft struck the shaft and the terrorists.

flash_696080.description: Following a rock attack on families traveling home, Yitzhar residents demand the IDF clear buildings and groves near the road to prevent further attacks.

flash_696077.description: Tzohar Rabbinical Organization releases a special prayer for Israel's elections, emphasizing national unity, shared responsibility, and mutual respect.

flash_696075.description: Lithuanian-haredi leader Rabbi Dov Lando says haredi 'Color Black' party uninterested in entering Knesset, will 'burn in hell.'

flash_696073.description: One day before the elections, Prof. Asher Cohen points to the gap in voter turnout between left-wing and right-wing strongholds, highlighting a factor that could determine the outcome.

flash_696071.description: Receiving five new ambassadors, Israeli President Isaac Herzog voices concern over Dutch criticism of Israel, while calling for stronger ties with France and expanded cooperation with Austria and African nations.

flash_696069.description: Searches following deadly terror attack reveal 15-meter-deep shaft near terrorist's home in Hebron, with electronic device inside.

flash_696104.description:
Syria's Border Crossings and Customs Authority announced the closure of the Nasib border crossing with Jordan following a Jordanian strike in southern Syria.

The authority said that passenger and cargo traffic through the crossing had been suspended in both directions.

flash_696103.description: Trump defends the war against Iran, warning that Tehran's missiles could threaten US cities: It should’ve been done a long time ago.

flash_696101.description: Israeli actress Gal Gadot receives an honorary doctorate from Bar-Ilan University, reflecting on October 7, Jewish unity and mutual responsibility while urging Israelis to vote.

flash_696099.description: President Trump denies reports that Netanyahu sought another endorsement ahead of Israel's election, while praising the Prime Minister's leadership and their joint actions against Iran.

flash_696095.description: United States President Donald Trump praised Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a conversation with reporters, saying: "Netanyahu has done a very good job as prime minister, under extremely challenging conditions."

flash_696093.description: A campaign ad from Cenk Uygur's PAC backing Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed sparked antisemitism accusations after blaming US grocery prices on aid to Israel.

flash_696089.description: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials meet Iranian leaders in Tehran to discuss de-escalation as Houthi attacks continue and Egypt backs Saudi defense.

flash_696087.description: Reuters reports that Hezbollah has received tens of millions of dollars from Iran to replenish its arsenal, develop explosive drones, and prepare for a possible renewal of fighting with Israel.

flash_696131.description:
Noam LeYisrael Party Chairman MK Avi Maoz cast his ballot at a polling station near his home in Jerusalem's Jewish Quarter. After voting, Maoz addressed what he described as a campaign being waged against his party, warning that it was expected to intensify throughout the day.

"Against the backdrop of the fake news campaign that has gained momentum over the past week, and based on information in our possession, we know that it is set to intensify further throughout the day," Maoz said.

He urged the public to ignore the "background noise" and emphasized: "Noam LeYisrael is staying in the race until the very end, and with God's help, we will be the surprise of the elections. Together, we will bring victory for Jewish education in the Jewish state."

flash_696130.description:
The Yisrael Beytenu Party has reported suspected election irregularities at polling station No. 45, located at 10 Gamla Street in Kiryat Ono. According to information received by the party, Yisrael Beytenu ballot slips, marked with the Hebrew letter Lamed (ל), have not been available at the polling station since it opened this morning.

Following the report, Yisrael Beytenu appealed to the Central Elections Committee, demanding that it investigate the incident and ensure the right of all voters to cast their ballots freely and equally.

flash_696128.description: President Isaac Herzog and First Lady Michal vote in Jerusalem, celebrating Israeli democracy and expressing hope for an Election Day free of disruptions.

flash_696126.description:
Asher Siman Tov, 103, who immigrated to Israel from Afghanistan and is one of the elders of the Orot HaTorah community in Bat Yam, arrived at a polling station this morning to exercise his democratic right to vote.

Siman Tov, who was able to participate in the elections even at his advanced age, voted for the Religious Zionist Party, placing a ballot marked with the Hebrew letter Tet (ט) in the ballot box.

Asher Siman Tov votes at 103Courtesy

flash_696123.description:
Shas Chairman Aryeh Deri warned of high voter turnout among left-wing and Arab voters, claiming that tens of thousands of Israelis had traveled from abroad specifically to participate in the elections and bring down the government.

"Unfortunately, voter turnout among the left and the Arabs is very high. Tens of thousands have arrived from abroad to vote and bring down the rule of the Torah," Deri said.

He added that, in light of the situation, "We must do everything possible to strengthen our position."

flash_696122.description:
Yashar Party Chairman Gadi Eisenkot began Election Day this morning at a polling station in Ofakim, alongside Shirel Hogeg, a local resident running on his party's slate.

"Today, we are embarking on a new path, with a shared future of healing and rebuilding. I call on everyone to vote for 'Derech' so that we will have the power to bring about change and a better future for all Israeli citizens," he said.

Later today, Eisenkot is expected to visit a polling station at Kibbutz Nir Oz, together with kibbutz member and former hostage Gadi Moses.

flash_696120.description: The NYPD is negotiating a $750,500 deal for Israeli-made AI phone-tracking technology, sparking privacy concerns.

flash_696118.description:
The Together Party filed a complaint with the Central Elections Committee, alleging that Likud representatives at polling stations are tracking voters and reporting information about them through an app, in violation of the law and the committee's guidelines.

The complaint was filed following documentation recorded by an election inspector in the Southern Sharon region, which the party claims provides evidence of this conduct.

flash_696116.description: Israel's Sephardic Chief Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef exercised his democratic right on Tuesday morning and cast his vote in Jerusalem.

flash_696114.description:
Polling stations across Israel are opening this morning for the elections to the 26th Knesset. Most polling stations will be open from 7:00 a.m. until 10:00 p.m.

In small communities and at polling stations located in hospitals, prisons, and nursing homes, voting will end earlier, at 8:00 p.m.

flash_696112.description: Netanyahu reportedly sought rabbis' help to persuade Ofer Winter to withdraw from the election. Rabbi David Abuhatzeira instead supports his candidacy.

flash_696110.description: The Justice Department files a new criminal case against former FBI Director James Comey over an alleged 2016 leak, triggering a dispute over filing deadlines.

flash_696108.description: Intel is acquiring Israeli quantum software company Classiq for $2.3 billion, marking a record deal for the industry and a milestone for Israel's technology sector.

flash_696106.description:
Syrian authorities reported that eight people, including three children, were killed in Jordanian airstrikes in the southern part of the country.

A Syrian health official said that four other people were wounded in the strikes.

flash_696102.description: Ambassador Danny Danon confronts UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese over her accusations against Israel and presents her with a resignation letter to sign: You are a disgrace to the UN.

flash_696181.description:
0:00 /

תיעוד חריג: מכות ליד קלפי ברהטלפי סעיף 27א

flash_696180.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich have just spoken and agreed to coordinate a joint effort to drive right-wing voters to the polls in the evening hours.

The conversation took place against the backdrop of the voting percentages in the Arab sector, which were described as worrying.

flash_696178.description: Amid long lines at polling stations, Israel's Central Elections Committee allows expired IDs and orders faster voting procedures and priority for disabled voters.

flash_696176.description: Channel 12's Amit Segal reports strong participation in Arab, center-left, and Likud strongholds.

flash_696174.description: 'Together' chairman Naftali Bennett, who attained control of Prime Minister's Office with just six Knesset seats in 2021, warns Israelis that party size does not matter - only bloc size matters.

flash_696172.description: IDF voter turnout by 1:00 p.m. at 48%

flash_696170.description:
The Central Elections Committee clarified that election officials may begin verifying the identity of the next voter in line while the current voter is behind the voting booth curtain casting their ballot, in an effort to reduce waiting times at polling stations.

The Director General of the Central Elections Committee warned: "Any polling station secretary who fails to prevent overcrowding will be dismissed from their position."

flash_696169.description:
Political commentator Amit Segal addressed the high voter turnout in strongholds of the Southern Faction of the Islamic Movement, arguing that it was the result of Mansour Abbas's early preparations for the elections. According to Segal, voter turnout in these strongholds is among the highest in the country.

Segal noted that the phenomenon is unusual even by international standards, with the poorest segment of society recording exceptionally high voter turnout. He added that, as of the time of his report, turnout in these areas was even higher than in the Haredi sector.

flash_696167.description: Security guards stop man approaching Democrats chairman Yair Golan, knife falls from suspect's clothing.

flash_696165.description:
Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg issued an interim order today prohibiting the United Torah Judaism faction and its representatives at polling stations from reporting the number of voters who have cast their ballots in real time.

The order was issued in response to a petition filed by the Movement for Quality Government in Israel against United Torah Judaism. The judge ordered the faction to submit its response by 2:15 p.m.

flash_696164.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, cast their ballots at a Jerusalem polling station

"This is a fateful moment; we know what is at stake. Vote for the future of the State of Israel," Netanyahu stated.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu votes in Israeli elections

flash_696163.description:
According to the latest voting figures, voter turnout stands at 28.6% in Tel Aviv, 26.8% in Jerusalem, and 26.6% in Haifa.

Among Israel's three largest cities, Tel Aviv leads in voter turnout, followed by Jerusalem and Haifa.

flash_696162.description: Ruby Chen, father of fallen soldier Itay Chen, is called a 'traitor' outside a Netanya polling station while urging Israelis to remember the fallen.

flash_696161.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog visits Central Elections Committee on Election Day, chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg wishes Israel 'great success.'

flash_696160.description: Acting Elections Committee Director: If lines continue past 10 p.m., voting will remain open

flash_696159.description: The word “choice," is not limited to the ballot box.

flash_696157.description: An Egyptian national who crossed into Israel near Nitzana is suspected of planning a terror attack; Shin Bet investigators identify possible nationalist motives.

flash_696155.description: Netherlands reverses its decision to return to Eurovision after Dutch broadcasters refuse to support participation alongside Israel.

flash_696153.description: Police arrest three Negev residents suspected of offering cash in exchange for votes for Ra'am in the Knesset elections.

flash_696206.description: Voter turnout figures as of 8:00 p.m. reveal significant differences between communities in Judea and Samaria.

flash_696205.description: Conservative commentator Mark Levin urges Likud and coalition supporters to get out and vote, warning that low turnout could put Israel's future and security at risk.

flash_696204.description: After a turbulent election day, the political drama reaches its climax: TV exit polls reveal the emerging distribution of Knesset seats and the balance of power between the political blocs.

flash_696202.description: Following a request by Likud, joined by Shas and Otzma Yehudit, the Central Elections Committee's presidium decided not to extend voting hours.

flash_696200.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s presidential election, has left the country for the US. Brazilian federal police are investigating, while Argentina denies he entered the country.

flash_696198.description:
The he Central Elections Committee decided to reject the request to extend voting hours at polling stations.

In accordance with the decision, the polling stations will close at 10:00 PM as planned, despite requests submitted by Likud and other parties due to congestion, long lines, and poor weather.

flash_696196.description: Media in Qatar, Lebanon, and Turkey focus on Arab voter turnout in Israel’s elections, while questioning whether a new government would change Israeli policy.

flash_696194.description: Polls open across Israel as 7.3 million eligible voters choose the next Knesset, with exit polls expected at 10 p.m. and a close race potentially ahead.

flash_696192.description: The IDF reports that as of 5:00 PM, the voting rate among those serving in the IDF stands at 68%, compared to 65% at the same time in the elections for the 25th Knesset.

flash_696190.description: Shas and United Torah Judaism campaign headquarters fear a loss of strength amid high voter turnout nationwide and are activating emergency operations to get voters to the polls.

flash_696188.description: Zehut leader Moshe Feiglin warns of a wide turnout gap between Arab voters and the national camp, urging eligible English speakers to vote to ensure national camp leadership.

flash_696186.description: Elections Committee Deputy Director General: Voter turnout may break 80% record

flash_696184.description: New York State Governor Kathy Hochul claims she is doing her best to protect Jewish New Yorkers and blames Netanyahu for the wave of antisemitism on Israel's election day.

flash_696182.description: Pollster Shlomo Filber predicts that unusually high voter turnout will make it harder for small parties to cross the electoral threshold.

flash_696179.description:
The Central Elections Committee clarified that a voter who encounters a damaged ballot should contact the polling clerk to receive a proper ballot.

In the event that a note from the requested list is missing, a white note can be used and the letters of the list can only be written on it in blue ink.

flash_696233.description:
Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot addressed senior officials in Israel's defense establishment and civil service, claiming that "Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister without a mandate or public trust."

Eisenkot urged senior officials to resist political pressure, stating, "Remember that you serve the state and the interests of Israel's citizens alone. You have my unequivocal backing."

Addressing Netanyahu directly, he declared, "Don't you dare use Israel's security for your political purposes."

flash_696232.description: Eisenkot: We made history, the public has voted against Netanyahu remaining in office

flash_696230.description: Channel 13 News released an updated election exit poll showing Likud gaining two seats to reach 27, while Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party loses one seat, dropping to 22.

flash_696229.description:
Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett responded to the election exit poll results, declaring, "People of Israel, hold your heads high. The alliance of those who serve has defeated the draft evaders."

Bennett added that "the October 7 government will be sent packing," expressing confidence that the current government would be replaced.

flash_696227.description: Religious Zionist Party chairman greeted with dancing at party headquarters, expresses hope that soldiers' votes would boost his party, and vows to continue Jewish settlement in Judea and Samaria and Gaza.

flash_696225.description: According to an updated election exit poll released by Channel 14, the right-wing bloc has increased its projected total to 62 Knesset seats.

flash_696223.description:
Otzma Yehudit chairman and Minister Itamar Ben Gvir responded to the exit poll results, warning against the formation of a unity government with Gadi Eisenkot. "This is exactly the scenario we warned against. It would be a terrible mistake," he said.

Ben Gvir expressed pride in his party's achievements and the support of hundreds of thousands of voters, adding, "I didn't enter politics to apologize for my principles, and I didn't come here to abandon the path I believe in."

flash_696222.description: Following disappointing exit polls, Winter vows to continue his political journey and rejects claims of wasted votes.

flash_696220.description: Liberman: There needs to be a revolt in the Likud, oust Netanyahu

flash_696218.description: The electoral threshold in the elections for the 26th Knesset was particularly high, requiring parties to receive approximately 186,000 votes to secure representation in the Knesset.

flash_696217.description: Eisenkot declares victory for the Zionist majority, Lapid speaks of a collapse, and Golan hails a historic opportunity. Zohar warns against a government backed by Arab parties.

flash_696215.description: Ofer Winter is expected to deliver a statement this evening at 11:25 p.m., following the release of exit polls for the 26th Knesset elections.

flash_696213.description: Kan 11 exit poll update: Bennett drops to 13 seats, while the Joint List rises to 11

flash_696211.description: Amit Segal outlines three possible scenarios following the exit poll results: a minority government, a unity government, or another election, saying that even a single Knesset seat could change the options for forming a government.

flash_696209.description:
According to the i24NEWS exit poll conducted by pollster Tzuriel Sharon, Likud leads with 27 seats, the Yashar Party receives 20 seats, and the Beyachad Party wins 15.

Yair Golan's party and the Joint List each receive 9 seats, Shas wins 8, and United Torah Judaism, Ra'am, and Otzma Yehudit each receive 7 seats.

Religious Zionism receives 6 seats, while Yisrael Beytenu wins 5 seats.

flash_696208.description:
According to Mano Geva's exit poll for Channel 12 News, Likud wins 24 seats, the Yashar Party 22, Bennett 12, the Joint List 11, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu 9 each, Shas 8, Ra'am 7, and United Torah Judaism, Ben Gvir's party, and Religious Zionism 6 seats each.

The parties led by Hendel, Zelekha, and Winter fail to cross the electoral threshold.

According to the exit poll, the Change Bloc stands at 52 seats, Netanyahu's bloc at 50 seats, and the Arab parties at 18 seats.

flash_696252.description:
According to partial official results of the elections for Israel's 26th Knesset, with approximately 37.4% of the votes counted, the current coalition drops to 57 seats, the change bloc rises to 47, and the Arab parties increase their combined representation to 16 seats. Likud loses one seat, falling to 28, while Yashar rises to 21 and the Joint List climbs to 12.

Together receives 11 seats, United Torah Judaism and Yisrael Beytenu eight each, while the Democrats, Otzma Yehudit, Shas, and the joint Religious Zionism-Zehut list each receive seven. Ra'am remains above the electoral threshold with 3.81% of the vote, giving it four seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.72% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.77%. These are partial results and may change as vote counting continues.

flash_696251.description: Minister Amichai Chikli criticizes those who predicted just 18 seats for Likud but stresses that it is still too early to declare an election victory.

flash_696250.description: Likud spokesman Guy Levy tells Arutz Sheva-Israel National News that exit polls point to a significant achievement for Netanyahu, but stresses that victory is not yet certain.

flash_696248.description:
According to the partial official results updated at 5:03 a.m., with approximately 31.2% of the votes counted, the distribution of political blocs remains unchanged: the current coalition holds 59 seats, the change bloc 46, and the Arab parties 15. Ra'am remains above the electoral threshold with 3.7% of the vote, giving it four seats.

In the distribution of seats, Likud leads with 29, followed by Yashar with 20, the Joint List and Together with 11 each, United Torah Judaism with nine, and Yisrael Beytenu with eight. Otzma Yehudit, the Democrats, Shas, and the joint Religious Zionism-Zehut list each receive seven seats.

The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.72% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.8%.

These are partial results and may change as vote counting continues.

flash_696247.description: With 28.2% of votes counted: Coalition drops to 59 seats, Ra'am crosses electoral threshold

flash_696246.description: Matan Kahana tells Arutz Sheva-Israel National News that Netanyahu's political career is over and makes clear that Yashar will not form a government dependent on Arab parties.

flash_696244.description: According to The Wall Street Journal, the US has warned Gulf Arab nations of a possible military offensive against Iran after the midterms.

flash_696242.description: The Central Elections Committee has begun releasing the official results of Israel's 26th Knesset elections. The figures are being updated as vote counting progresses.

flash_696240.description: Netanyahu: Thanks to our heroic soldiers, we have achieved wonders that changed the Middle East

flash_696238.description: Netanyahu takes the stage to deliver speech at Jerusalem Convention Center

flash_696236.description: According to the latest update to Channel 12 News' exit poll for Israel's 26th Knesset elections, Netanyahu's bloc has strengthened to 52 seats, while Eisenkot's bloc is projected to win 49 seats. The Arab parties are projected to receive 19 seats.

flash_696235.description: Zehut chairman warns of growing Arab party influence, presents his party as the answer to Israel's identity crisis, and sets his sights on the Defense Ministry.

flash_696231.description: Geffen Brailovsky, head of Amcha Yisrael's youth campaign, tells Arutz Sheva-Israel National News she believes the official election results will tell a different story.

flash_696228.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to arrive at the International Convention Center in Jerusalem in approximately an hour to deliver a speech following the release of the election exit polls and the start of the official vote count.

flash_696226.description:
The Central Elections Committee announced that the first official results of the elections for the 26th Knesset have begun to be released.

The results will be updated throughout the night as vote counting and verification progress. The committee emphasized that the figures are preliminary and partial and may change.

flash_696224.description:
Channel 14 released an updated election exit poll showing that Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu party would fail to cross the electoral threshold.

As a result, Netanyahu's bloc has risen to 61 seats, securing a majority sufficient to form a government, according to the updated exit poll.
